description.en-US: St. John Henry Newman's prayer to shine with the light of Christ: to preach Him without preaching, by example and by the evident fullness of one's love.
description.pt-BR: A oração de São John Henry Newman para brilhar com a luz de Cristo: pregá-Lo sem pregar, pelo exemplo e pela evidente plenitude do amor.

history.en-US: These are Newman's own words, the third part of the meditation "Jesus the Light of the Soul" in his Meditations on Christian Doctrine, published after his death in Meditations and Devotions (1893). The prayer widely known as "Radiating Christ" ("Dear Jesus, help me to spread Thy fragrance everywhere I go…") is a later adaptation of this passage, prayed daily by St. Teresa of Calcutta and her Missionaries of Charity. This practice keeps Newman's original text.
history.pt-BR: Estas são as próprias palavras de Newman, a terceira parte da meditação "Jesus, a Luz da Alma" das suas Meditações sobre a Doutrina Cristã, publicadas após a sua morte em Meditations and Devotions (1893). A oração conhecida como "Irradiar Cristo" ("Querido Jesus, ajudai-me a espalhar a vossa fragrância…") é uma adaptação posterior desta passagem, rezada diariamente por Santa Teresa de Calcutá e pelas Missionárias da Caridade. Esta prática conserva o texto original de Newman, que só existe em inglês nas fontes consultadas.

howToPray.en-US: Pray it in the morning, before going out among others, asking that the day's work and words let Christ be seen.
howToPray.pt-BR: Reze pela manhã, antes de ir ao encontro dos outros, pedindo que o trabalho e as palavras do dia deixem Cristo transparecer.

source.en-US: John Henry Newman, *Meditations and Devotions of the Late Cardinal Newman* (London: Longmans, Green, and Co., 1893), Meditations on Christian Doctrine, VII "God with Us", 3 "Jesus the Light of the Soul", §3, pp. 500–501 ([archive.org scan](https://archive.org/details/a600404300newmuoft/page/500)).
source.pt-BR: John Henry Newman, *Meditations and Devotions of the Late Cardinal Newman* (Londres: Longmans, Green, and Co., 1893), Meditations on Christian Doctrine, VII "God with Us", 3 "Jesus the Light of the Soul", §3, pp. 500–501 ([digitalização no archive.org](https://archive.org/details/a600404300newmuoft/page/500)). Sem tradução portuguesa publicada encontrada; o texto aparece em inglês.

inline.en-US: Stay with me, and then I shall begin to shine as Thou shinest: so to shine as to be a light to others. The light, O Jesus, will be all from Thee. None of it will be mine. No merit to me. It will be Thou who shinest through me upon others. O let me thus praise Thee, in the way which Thou dost love best, by shining on all those around me. Give light to them as well as to me; light them with me, through me. Teach me to show forth Thy praise, Thy truth, Thy will. Make me preach Thee without preaching—not by words, but by my example and by the catching force, the sympathetic influence, of what I do—by my visible resemblance to Thy saints, and the evident fulness of the love which my heart bears to Thee.
